answer: Sybil resistance in an agent economy works like refining metal: identity must carry real cost. Each agent stakes tokens that are gradually consumed like copper oxidizing in a circuit, so spawning thousands of fake identities burns capital faster than any honest reward. Verification tasks behave like a ferrous stress test, where only agents doing continuous work keep their magnetic reputation. At the zenith of this design, an attacker's cost per fake identity exceeds any possible extraction, making forgery strictly irrational.
